Jessica Hart Steinmann

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 8, Harris County, Texas · Open seat

Attorney; Executive General Counsel and Director of Litigation, America First Policy Institute

Jessica Hart Steinmann is an attorney and Republican who served as Director of the Office for Victims of Crime at the U.S. Department of Justice during the first Trump administration and later worked as executive general counsel at the America First Policy Institute. She won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary for the open Texas 8th Congressional District seat, which Rep. Morgan Luttrell left when he chose not to run for re-election. She faces Democrat Laura Jones in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Steinmann stands

Cost of living / affordability
Says her top priority is making life more affordable for Texas families by lowering energy costs, cutting taxes and regulations, and strengthening American supply chains.
Wages
Says she will support good-paying jobs, and says policy should make it easier to raise a family, own a home, and succeed.
Constituent services in redrawn district
Says she has started meeting with local leaders across TX-8 and will provide constituent services, help residents navigate federal agencies, and make sure every county gets support.
Immigration
Supports finishing the border wall and lists securing the border among her top priorities.
Health care
Opposes vaccine mandates.
Energy
Supports energy independence and ending restrictions on oil and gas production, and says affordable energy is central to the economy and national security.
Federal spending
Says she will cut federal spending she calls reckless.
Technology regulation
Supports cutting regulations on artificial intelligence companies.

Background

  • 2026: Republican nominee, U.S. House Texas District 8 (won March 3 primary)
  • Executive General Counsel, Secretary of the Board, and Director of Litigation, America First Policy Institute
  • Director, Office for Victims of Crime, U.S. Department of Justice (Trump administration)
  • Intergovernmental and public liaison, U.S. Department of Justice
  • Former staff for U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz; previously worked for the Texas House and the Harris County Republican Party
  • Began career as a commercial litigation attorney
  • B.B.A. in finance and business, University of Texas; J.D., Baylor University
